```{r}
nrow(data)  # Should return a positive number
ncol(data)
sapply(data, class)
# Check for missing values
sum(is.na(data))
apply(data, 2, var)
if (nrow(data) > 0 && ncol(data) > 0) {
  # Check if there are any non-numeric columns
  column_classes <- sapply(data, class)
  print(column_classes)

  # Remove non-numeric columns or convert them
  data_numeric <- data[, sapply(data, is.numeric)]

  # Check for NA values
  sum(is.na(data_numeric))  # If any, handle them (remove or impute)

  # Calculate the variance of each numeric column
  column_variances <- apply(data_numeric, 2, var)
  print(column_variances)
} else {
  print("The data frame is empty or has no valid rows/columns.")
}
```

```{r}
data$zero_flag <- as.integer(data$Nephtyidae == 0.0)

# Separate the data into two parts:
# 1. Binary model: Predict if the target is zero
# 2. Regression model: Predict the target value when it's non-zero
model <- lm(zero_flag ~ ., data = data)
# Binary model to predict zero vs non-zero
binary_data <- data[data$zero_flag %in% c(0, 1), ]
binary_model <- bartMachine(
  data[, colnames(data) != "Nephtyidae" & colnames(data) != "zero_flag"],
  data[, "zero_flag"],
  seed = 42,
  num_trees = 50,
  num_burn_in = 250,
  num_iterations_after_burn_in = 1000,
  mh_prob_steps = c(2.5, 2.5, 4)/9,
)
binary_model
# Regression model for predicting the value of Nephtyidae when it's non-zero
regression_model <- bartMachine(
  binary_data[, colnames(data) != "Nephtyidae" & colnames(data) != "zero_flag"],
  binary_data$Nephtyidae,
  seed = 42,
  num_trees = 80,
  num_burn_in = 250,
  num_iterations_after_burn_in = 1000,
  mh_prob_steps = c(2.5, 2.5, 4)/9,
  mem_cache_for_speed = FALSE
)

# Now make predictions for both models

# Predict the probability of zero (binary model)
binary_pred <- predict(binary_model, new_data = data[, colnames(data) != "Nephtyidae" & colnames(data) != "zero_flag"])
predictions_binary <- ifelse(binary_pred > 0.5, 1, 0)
# Predict the actual target values (regression model)
regression_pred <- predict(regression_model, new_data = data[, colnames(data) != "Nephtyidae" & colnames(data) != "zero_flag"])

# Combine the predictions
# If the binary model predicts zero, we assign the target as 0, else we use the regression prediction
final_predictions <- ifelse(predictions_binary == 1, 0, regression_pred)
final_predictions
# Evaluation (e.g., RMSE or R-squared)
rmse <- sqrt(mean((final_predictions - data$Nephtyidae)^2))
print(paste("RMSE:", rmse))

ss_total <- sum((data$Nephtyidae - mean(data$Nephtyidae))^2)
ss_residual <- sum((data$Nephtyidae - final_predictions)^2)
r_squared <- 1 - (ss_residual / ss_total)
print(paste("R-squared:", r_squared))
```

```{r}
model <- wbart(
  x.train = X_train,    # Predictor variables
  y.train = y_train$Nephtyidae,      # Target variable
  nskip = 1000,            # Burn-in iterations
  ndpost = 2000,           # Number of posterior samples
  ntree = 100              # Number of trees in the ensemble (default: 200)
)

# Model summary
summary(model)

# Make predictions on training data
predictions <- predict(model, X_train)
predictions <- apply(predictions, 2, mean)

# Calculate RMSE on the training data
rmse <- sqrt(mean((y_train - predictions)^2))
cat("RMSE: ", rmse, "\n")

# Plot predicted vs actual values
plot(y_train$Nephtyidae,predictions, main = "BART: Predicted vs Actual")
```
```{r}
num_trees_values <- c(50, 100, 200)
num_burn_values <- c(1000, 2000)
num_post_values <- c(2000, 3000)

results <- data.frame(num_trees = numeric(), num_burn = numeric(), num_post = numeric(), rmse = numeric())

# Grid search loop
for (num_trees in num_trees_values) {
  for (num_burn in num_burn_values) {
    for (num_post in num_post_values) {
      
      # Fit BART model with current parameters
      model <- bart(
        x.train = X_train, 
        y.train = y_train$Nephtyidae, 
        ntree = num_trees, 
        nskip = num_burn, 
        ndpost = num_post,
        keeptrees = TRUE,              # Keep the trees for prediction
        k = 2    
      )
      
      # Make predictions and calculate RMSE
      predictions <- predict(model, X_train)
      rmse <- sqrt(mean((y_train$Nephtyidae - predictions)^2))
      
      # Store results
      results <- rbind(results, data.frame(num_trees = num_trees, num_burn = num_burn, num_post = num_post, rmse = rmse))
    }
  }
}

# View the results and find the best parameters
print(results)

# Best parameters based on RMSE
best_model_params <- results[which.min(results$rmse), ]
print(best_model_params)
```
